transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I've been having this issue with eating. After my late shifts, I'll stop to grab some food, but then... I just keep going once I get home. I'll eat a full takeout meal, and then move on to chips, sweets, just whatever’s around the apartment. And afterward, I look around and I'm honestly just shocked by how much I actually ate. It's starting to really bother me, so I figured I should talk to someone.
After eating like that, do you do anything to try to make up for the food or prevent weight gain, such as making yourself vomit?

Yeah, I do. Um, sometimes after I eat too much of that takeout or the snacks, I'll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just... I do it so all that food won't just sit in me and turn into extra weight.
Could you tell me what your current height and weight are?
I'm about 5'10", and the last time I checked, I was around 165 pounds.
On average, how many times a week do these episodes of overeating and making yourself throw up happen?

Well, since the apartment move settled into a routine, I'd say... most weeks I have at least one late-night episode where I eat way past what I meant to. And then to try and make up for it, I'll throw up, or sometimes I'll skip breakfast the next morning, or just force myself to go on a really long run.
For how many months have you been having these episodes of overeating and making up for them?
I'd say it's been going on for... about a year and five months now. It started right around the time I moved into that temporary apartment down near the tourist district.
How much does your body shape or weight influence how you feel about yourself as a person?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean... I care about my weight, obviously, but I don't know if I've ever really noticed it changing how I feel about myself as a whole person. I just get frustrated when I feel out of shape, but I couldn't really tell you how much it actually influences my overall self-worth. I just haven't really thought about it in those terms.
During these times when you're eating so much food, do you feel like you've lost control, such as feeling unable to stop eating or control what you're eating?

Yeah, I definitely do. It's... well, once I start on those nights, it’s almost like I’m watching myself from the outside. I'll be in my head telling myself to just put the food away, but my hands just keep opening containers. I just keep going until everything is gone, and I can't really stop it.
Would you say you have an intense, overwhelming dread or fear of becoming fat?

Yeah, I would. Honestly, it's... it's a huge fear of mine. Even when people at the venue where I work tell me I look too lean, I still get really panicky if my pants feel even a little tighter or if the scale goes up just a pound. I just get this overwhelming feeling like all the guests and my coworkers are going to notice right away and think I've completely let myself go. It's always in the back of my mind.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). He describes recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by consuming large amounts of food with a subjective loss of control, accompanied by recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors including self-induced vomiting, fasting, and excessive exercise to prevent weight gain. These behaviors have persisted at an average frequency of at least once per week for approximately 1 year and 5 months. He also endorses a morbid dread of becoming fat, while maintaining a normal body weight (BMI approx. 23.7 kg/m²), ruling out anorexia nervosa.
